api: AffineRowReader(checkpoint, identity, expected_sha256=...).read(rows) -> raw unique-row bytes, request mapping and receipt
CLI bind/read; read prints receipts only, never raw payloads
guarantees: Config/index and exact selected physical-shard ownership validated; weight/scales/biases must share one shard.
Selected spans regenerated from existing affine planner, with bits2/3/4/5/6/8, groups32/64/128, U32 packed weights and same-dtype F16/BF16/F32 metadata.
Canonical external identity pin, implementation hashes, metadata/header/stat bindings, descriptor checks at open and after I/O, opened-header hash, and every selected component hash before returning.
Duplicate requests incur no repeated payload reads; unbound rows and exceeded budgets fail before selected payload reads.
Binding and reads each perform exactly one pread per unique row/component, plus one bounded opened-header verification; no complete shard scan or decoded allocation.

budget_contract.metadata_accounting: 8MiB budget is tensor payload only; metadata uses separately capped reads. Opened-header verification byte count is explicit in bind/read receipts; metadata inspection also reads header/config/index during bind/constructor.

limitations: Raw storage bytes only: no decode/finiteness assertion for affine values, native MLX integration, actual model payload, GPU, numerical forward/VJP or training qualification.
Only selected payload hashes are established. No full-file payload SHA is computed, and no duplicate-name audit of unselected physical shards occurs.
Bindings are local inode/stat/source-bound consistency identities, not portable/authenticated model provenance. Rebinding explicitly rereads selected bytes after replacement or implementation change.
All tests use synthetic temporary shards. The current architecture remains unsupported for end-to-end Qwen model execution/training.
